decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a growing niche in which there are few competitors, and its US release in 2019 leaves its value still unfolding, so keeping this low-cost option open is justified.
Demand for small-field dosimetry keeps rising and a chamber costs little to carry, while nothing observed signals that its value will fail to materialize.
Despite some overlap with B, the second small volume chamber has no evidence against it and costs little to keep, so the option stays open.
The standard clinical chamber line is a core dosimetry product tied to recurring calibration and service revenue, making it a committed investment rather than an option to abandon.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantom scanning workflow that supports the platform strategy, and it is cheap to maintain.
Thimble chambers are established devices with predictable demand, and no results suggest that this one should be abandoned.
